Several statements are wrong or unsupported, and the next steps are weak, so an investigator would have to redo some of the work.","problems":["The headline says 99215 is billed at \"roughly twice the all-provider rate in every complexity band\". The card shows ratios of about 1.9x, 2.3x, 2.3x, 1.8x, 1.8x and 1.6x, so \"roughly twice\" overstates the top bands and is imprecise.","The rationale says the J06.9 low-complexity visits would rarely need high-complexity decision-making, and that this \"fits a pattern consistent with upcoding\". That is inference from diagnosis codes alone and is somewhat leading given the inconclusive stance.","The comparison \"against 5% for the comparison providers\" is correct for 99215 (all_provider_rate 0.048). The \"above-peer below-billed rate\" for 99214 (2 of 22, 9.1% vs 3.0%) rests on a tiny sample and is weak.","\"Repeated time entries\" is not on the evidence card, and neither is the note-checks line (problems 20%, late 0%, unsigned 0%, data 3%). Both would have to come from tool output and are unverifiable here.","The next step names C0025608 and C0025694 as 99215 charts to request, but they are 99214 claims already returned and documented, so the citation does not fit the step. The headline recommendation, to request charts for the low-complexity J06.9 and Z09 99215 claims, is not carried into the next steps.","The next steps are generic. They do not name the J06.9 claims, and they omit the audit trail request that appears in the rationale.","The summary is repetitive: the audit trail and the 3 data-reviewed notes are each mentioned twice."]}
